setting.tex:
The risk of a language $L$ is $\err_\cD(L)=\Pr_{x\sim\cD}[x\notin L]$, and its empirical risk is $\err_S(L)=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\one\{x_t\notin L\}$.
An identification algorithm $\cA$ maps a sample to a language in $\cC$, and a generation algorithm maps it to a string in $\cU$.
Both can use internal randomness.

Let $\eps>0$ and $\delta\ge0$.
A randomized algorithm $\cA:\cU^n\to\cR$ is \emph{$(\eps,\delta)$-DP}~\citep{dmns06} if $\Pr[\cA(S)\in F]\le e^{\eps}\Pr[\cA(S')\in F]+\delta$ for all neighbors $S,S'$ and every measurable $F\subseteq\cR$.
It is \emph{$\eps$-DP} (pure DP) if $\delta=0$.
We call every algorithm $\infty$-DP.

quotes.tex:
Let Assumption~\ref{asm:attained} hold, and let $f(n)\to\infty$.
For every $n$ with $f(n)\ge\max\{i^\star,3/\cgap,3\}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item for every $\eps>0$, the exponential-mechanism identifier is $\eps$-DP and
\[
\iderr\le2f\,e^{-n/(8f^2)}+f\,e^{-\eps n/(4f)};
\]
\item for every $\eps,\delta\in(0,1)$, the Gaussian identifier is $(\eps,\delta)$-DP and
\[
\iderr\le2f\,e^{-n/(8f^2)}+2f\exp\Bigl(-\frac{\eps^2n^2}{64f^3\log(1.25/\delta)}\Bigr).
\]
\end{enumerate}

terms.tex:
Some index $i$ satisfies $\err_\cD(L_i)=\inf_{L\in\cC}\err_\cD(L)$.
We call the smallest such index the \emph{target index} $i^\star$.
If $i^\star>1$, the earlier languages are strictly worse, and we write $\cgap=\min_{j<i^\star}\bigl(\err_\cD(L_j)-\err_\cD(L_{i^\star})\bigr)>0$; if $i^\star=1$, we set $\cgap=1$.

quotes.tex:
Let Assumption~\ref{asm:gen} hold, and let $W\ge w$ be public.
For every $n$ with $f(n)\ge i^\star$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item for every $\eps>0$, the exponential-mechanism generator is $\eps$-DP and
\[
\generr\le W e^{-nm_W/8}+f\,e^{-\eps nm_W/4}+n2^{-n};
\]
\item for every $\eps,\delta\in(0,1)$, the Gaussian generator is $(\eps,\delta)$-DP and
\[
\generr\le W e^{-nm_W/8}+2f\exp\Bigl(-\frac{\eps^2n^2m_W^2}{64f\log(1.25/\delta)}\Bigr)+n2^{-n}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

terms.tex:
Fix an enumeration $\cU=\{u_1,u_2,\dots\}$, and let $\cU_\ell=\{u_1,\dots,u_\ell\}$ be its first $\ell$ strings; we call $\ell$ a \emph{level}.
Assume that every language in $\cC$ is infinite.
A language $L_i$ is \emph{good} if $L_i\subseteq\supp(\cD)$ and \emph{bad} otherwise.
A good language is a safe source of valid strings, and a bad language contains a string outside the support.
The \emph{witness index} $w=w(\cC,\cD)$ is the smallest level $w\in\N$ such that every bad language contains a string of $\cU_w$ outside $\supp(\cD)$.
If there is no such level, then $w=\infty$.

(a) The witness index is finite.
(b) Some language in $\cC$ is good; the \emph{target index} $i^\star$ is the smallest such index.

One number of the distribution governs all rates below: the \emph{mass floor} at level $\ell$,
\[
m_\ell=\min_{u\in L_{i^\star}\cap\,\cU_\ell}\cD(u)\qquad(\text{and }m_\ell=1\text{ if }L_{i^\star}\cap\cU_\ell=\varnothing),
\]
the smallest probability of a target string among the first $\ell$ strings.
It is positive because the target language is good, and it does not increase with $\ell$.

quotes.tex:
Let Assumption~\ref{asm:gen} hold, and use the profile $\lambda_\ell=g\,\ell/(\ell+1)$.
For every $n$ with $f(n)\ge i^\star$ and $0<g(n)\le nm_w/2$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item for every $\eps>0$, the exponential-mechanism generator is $\eps$-DP and
\[
\generr\le w e^{-nm_w/8}+f\exp\Bigl(-\frac{\eps g}{2w(w+1)}\Bigr)+n2^{-n};
\]
\item for every $\eps,\delta\in(0,1)$, the Gaussian generator is $(\eps,\delta)$-DP and
\[
\generr\le w e^{-nm_w/8}+2f\exp\Bigl(-\frac{\eps^2g^2}{16\,w^2(w+1)^2f\log(1.25/\delta)}\Bigr)+n2^{-n}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

terms.tex:
Fix an enumeration $\cU=\{u_1,u_2,\dots\}$, and let $\cU_\ell=\{u_1,\dots,u_\ell\}$ be its first $\ell$ strings; we call $\ell$ a \emph{level}.
Assume that every language in $\cC$ is infinite.
A language $L_i$ is \emph{good} if $L_i\subseteq\supp(\cD)$ and \emph{bad} otherwise.
A good language is a safe source of valid strings, and a bad language contains a string outside the support.
The \emph{witness index} $w=w(\cC,\cD)$ is the smallest level $w\in\N$ such that every bad language contains a string of $\cU_w$ outside $\supp(\cD)$.
If there is no such level, then $w=\infty$.

A \emph{cap profile} is a nondecreasing map $\lambda:\N\cup\{0\}\to[0,\infty]$ with $\lambda_0=0$.
The capped-depth score of $L_i$ is
\[
\qgen(S,i)=\max_{\ell\in\N}\ \min\bigl\{a_{i,\ell}(S),\,\lambda_\ell\bigr\}.
\]

One number of the distribution governs all rates below: the \emph{mass floor} at level $\ell$,
\[
m_\ell=\min_{u\in L_{i^\star}\cap\,\cU_\ell}\cD(u)\qquad(\text{and }m_\ell=1\text{ if }L_{i^\star}\cap\cU_\ell=\varnothing),
\]
the smallest probability of a target string among the first $\ell$ strings.
It is positive because the target language is good, and it does not increase with $\ell$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\cC$ be finite, and let it contain two infinite languages $L,L'$ with $L\cap L'$ finite.
Let $\eps\in(0,\infty)$, and let $\cA$ be an $\eps$-DP generator whose error tends to $0$ for every distribution that satisfies Assumption~\ref{asm:gen}.
Then every distribution $\cD$ with $\supp(\cD)=L$ satisfies, for every $c>0$,
\[
\generr(\cA,\cD,\cC,n)\;\ge\;\tfrac12\,e^{-cn}\qquad\text{for all large }n.
\]
The same holds for $(\eps,\delta_n)$-DP generators if $\delta_n\le e^{-c_0n}$ for some $c_0>0$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\cC$ satisfy the IPP condition.
There are two distributions $\cD_0,\cD_1$ that satisfy Assumption~\ref{asm:attained}, such that for every $\eps\in(0,\infty]$, every $\eps$-DP identification algorithm $\cA$, and every $n\ge1$,
\[
\max_{b\in\{0,1\}}\iderr(\cA,\cD_b,\cC,n)\;\ge\;\frac18\Bigl(1-\frac{\theta_\eps}4\Bigr)^n\;\ge\;\frac18\,e^{-\min\{1,\eps\}\,n/3}.
\]

terms.tex:
A collection $\cC$ satisfies the \emph{intersecting private-pair} (IPP) condition if it contains two languages $L\ne L'$ with $L\cap L'\ne\varnothing$, and each of them contains a \emph{private} string.
A string is private to $L$ if no other language of $\cC$ contains it.
A coupled pair of samples then differs in each coordinate with probability $1/4$, and the bound is $(1-\theta_\eps/4)^n$ with $\theta_\eps=1-e^{-\eps}$.

quotes.tex:
Let $\cC$ satisfy the IIDP condition.
There are two distributions $\cD_0,\cD_1$ such that for every $\eps\in(0,\infty]$, every $\eps$-DP generation algorithm $\cA$, and every $n\ge1$,
\[
\max_{b\in\{0,1\}}\generr(\cA,\cD_b,\cC,n)\;\ge\;\frac13\Bigl(1-\frac{\theta_\eps}4\Bigr)^n\;\ge\;\frac13\,e^{-\min\{1,\eps\}\,n/3}.
\]

terms.tex: A collection $\cC$ satisfies the \emph{intersecting infinite-difference pair} (IIDP) condition if it contains two languages $L,L'$ with $L\cap L'\ne\varnothing$ such that $L\setminus L'$ and $L'\setminus L$ are infinite.
A coupled pair of samples then differs in each coordinate with probability $1/4$, and the bound is $(1-\theta_\eps/4)^n$ with $\theta_\eps=1-e^{-\eps}$.
